prompt.context_jp: 新年を迎えた朝の光が、群馬県庁前の広場に静かに満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新年を迎えた朝の光（　）、群馬県庁前の広場に静かに満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the opening scene description?

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-setting opening sentence introducing new visual information. が presents the morning light as fresh, observable information filling the square.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 'the morning light' as an already-known topic, which doesn't match an opening descriptive line that paints the scene.

prompt.context_jp: 号砲が上州の空気を鋭く切り裂いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 号砲が上州の空気（　）鋭く切り裂いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what gets cut.

feedback.correct_en: 切り裂く is a transitive verb; the air is the direct object being sliced through, so を is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would create a second subject and break the sentence; に would mark a destination, not what's being cut.

prompt.context_jp: ここから先は、こはぜ屋の技術が世に問われる百キロだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ここから先（　）、こはぜ屋の技術が世に問われる百キロだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 'ここから先'.

feedback.correct_en: 'ここから先' is set up as the topic/frame for the rest of the sentence — 'as for from here on...' は marks this scope-setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 'ここから先' as new information identifying a subject, but the predicate instead describes what this stretch amounts to; it needs topic framing.

prompt.context_jp: 外国人ランナーが躍り出て、風景そのものが一段早回しになったようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 外国人ランナー（　）躍り出て、風景そのものが一段早回しになったようだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing the Kenyan runner's burst.

feedback.correct_en: The foreign runner's sudden burst forward is new, event-reporting information — a classic が use for introducing something happening in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the runner as an already-established topic, losing the sense of a sudden, visible event.

prompt.context_jp: 立原の姿がモニターに大きく映し出され、宮沢は思わず前のめりになった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 立原の姿（　）モニターに大きく映し出され、宮沢は思わず前のめりになった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Tachihara's image appearing on the monitor.

feedback.correct_en: Tachihara's figure appearing on the monitor is a new scene event triggering Miyazawa's reaction. が reports this fresh visual.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Tachihara's figure' an established theme, losing the sudden-on-screen feel that motivates Miyazawa's leaning forward.

prompt.context_jp: 監督の顔からは、みるみる血の気が引いていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 監督の顔から（　）、みるみる血の気が引いていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle attaching to から.

feedback.correct_en: から marks the source; stacking は highlights 'from the coach's face (in particular)' as the topic/contrast scope for 血の気が引く.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot attach after から here; を would make no sense since から is already marking the source phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔からは血の気が引いた。
contrast_examples.en: The color drained from his face (topicalized).

prompt.context_jp: 「ニューイヤーでは2区だけが外国人選手も走れる規定になったんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: ニューイヤーで（　）2区だけが外国人選手も走れる規定になったんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 'で' here.

feedback.correct_en: では contrasts this race (the New Year ekiden) against other races — the special rule applies here (unlike elsewhere). は on top of で signals that contrastive scope.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot attach to で like this; the sentence needs a scope-setting/contrast marker, not a new-subject marker.

contrast_examples.en: In Japan (as opposed to elsewhere), cherry blossoms bloom.

prompt.context_jp: 「ダイワは 1 2 3 4… 5位かな」「5位か よーし 悪くない」
prompt.prompt_jp: ダイワ（　）5位だ。
prompt.prompt_en: The announcer identifies which place Daiwa is in. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The topic is Daiwa (already established as the team of interest) and the comment supplies their rank. は is natural: 'As for Daiwa, 5th'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is in 5th place?' with exhaustive-listing force — but the speaker is reporting Daiwa's position, not identifying who holds 5th.

prompt.context_jp: 応援旗を横一線に押し倒すほどの風が、沿道に吹き始めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 応援旗を横一線に押し倒すほどの風（　）、沿道に吹き始めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the wind arriving on scene.

feedback.correct_en: A strong wind suddenly begins to blow — a brand-new event in the scene. が reports this new occurrence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'such a wind' as an already-known topic, which clashes with the setup of the wind just now starting.

prompt.context_jp: それは紛れもなく、こはぜ屋が刻んだ陸王のシルエットだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: それ（　）紛れもなく、こはぜ屋が刻んだ陸王のシルエットだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'それ' identifying the shoe.

feedback.correct_en: 'それ' refers back to the fluorescent color at Mogi's feet — a known referent. The sentence then asserts what it is. Topic-comment calls for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight 'それ' as new identifying information, but the sentence structure is X は Y だった (definition of a known X).

contrast_examples.en: This is Rikuoh (identifying the known this).
THIS is Rikuoh (exhaustive — out of options, this one).

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢は無言のまま画面を追い、大地は隣で唇を噛みしめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宮沢は無言のまま画面を追い、大地（　）隣で唇を噛みしめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for '大地' in the second clause.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence pairs two people and contrasts what each is doing: Miyazawa does X, Daichi (meanwhile) does Y. Contrastive は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Daichi as the new discovered doer of an event, losing the parallel 'A does X, B does Y' contrast with Miyazawa.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄は本を読み、弟は寝ていた。
contrast_examples.en: The older brother read; the younger slept (contrast).
The younger brother was sleeping (new info).

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢の口の中は、からからに乾いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宮沢の口の中（　）、からからに乾いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after '宮沢の口の中'.

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic 'X の Y は〜' body-state description: focus is on Miyazawa, and his mouth's condition is described. は marks the topic/scope.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as newly identifying 'what is dry' — but the narrator is already zoomed in on Miyazawa and simply reports his state.

prompt.context_jp: 茂木の脚は、まだ止まる気配を見せない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 茂木の脚（　）、まだ止まる気配を見せない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for '茂木の脚'.

feedback.correct_en: Mogi is already the focal runner; the narrator comments on his legs as the topic ('as for Mogi's legs...'). は fits the ongoing description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present his legs as new information just discovered, but the sentence is a continued commentary on an already-tracked runner.

prompt.context_jp: スピーカーから流れる実況の声が、いよいよ号砲を告げようとしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: スピーカー（　）流れる実況の声が、いよいよ号砲を告げようとしている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 'スピーカー'.

feedback.correct_en: The voice comes OUT OF the speaker — から marks the source point from which the sound flows.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the speaker as a means/location of action but 流れる (to flow) specifically takes a source with から. を doesn't fit intransitive 流れる.

contrast_examples.jp: ラジオから音が流れる。

contrast_examples.en: Listen to music via the radio (means).

prompt.context_jp: あけみと美咲は沿道で思わず口を押さえた。
prompt.prompt_jp: あけみと美咲は沿道（　）思わず口を押さえた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for '沿道'.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location WHERE an action takes place — Akemi and Misaki's action of covering their mouths happens along the roadside.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark existence or a destination, not the setting of a performed action. を doesn't mark a location.

prompt.context_jp: 翌日、宮沢は寮に茂木を訪ねた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 翌日、宮沢は寮（　）茂木を訪ねた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for '寮'.

feedback.correct_en: 訪ねる takes に to mark the place one visits/goes to. The dorm is the destination of Miyazawa's visit.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark an action location, but 訪ねる is directed at a destination. を doesn't fit this pattern.

prompt.context_jp: 「茂木が陸王 履いたって お前がメールで知らせてくるからさ　＿＿＿＿なっちまったよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: いても　＿＿＿＿　いられなくなっちまったよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom meaning 'couldn't just sit still'.

feedback.correct_en: いてもたってもいられない is a fixed idiom meaning 'can't bear to just sit (or stand) still' from excitement/worry. The advisor had to come see it.
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom specifically pairs いる (to sit/be) with たつ (to stand); other verbs don't form this set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: いてもたってもいられない。

prompt.context_jp: 立原は最近 連戦でしたからね ここで そのツケが＿＿＿＿きたな
prompt.prompt_jp: そのツケが　＿＿＿＿　きたな。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb for 'the bill came due / the consequences caught up'.

feedback.correct_en: ツケが回ってくる is the set expression for 'the bill/consequences come around' — overexertion finally caught up with Tachihara.
feedback.incorrect_en: 届く or 通る don't form this idiom with ツケ; only 回る captures the sense of consequences circling back.

contrast_examples.jp: 無理したツケが回ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: The bill for overdoing it came due.

prompt.context_jp: 「茂木が 一気に前に出ます すばらしい ＿＿＿＿ってますね」
prompt.prompt_jp: すばらしい　神　＿＿＿＿　ってますね。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb form for 'possessed by a god / otherworldly'.

feedback.correct_en: 神懸かる means to be in a divinely inspired, superhuman state — perfect for Mogi's uncanny run.
feedback.incorrect_en: 神頼みis a different phrase (praying to gods), and 預かる (take custody of) makes no sense here.

contrast_examples.en: Pray to the gods for help.

prompt.context_jp: 向かい風の中で わざと毛塚の後ろを走ることで 体力を　＿＿＿＿し 残り1キロに 勝負をかけたんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 体力を　＿＿＿＿　し、残り1キロに勝負をかけたんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb meaning 'conserve/preserve' stamina.

feedback.correct_en: 体力を温存する is the standard collocation for 'conserve stamina' — holding something in reserve for later use.
feedback.incorrect_en: 保管 is for storing physical objects, and 保存 is for preserving data/food. Neither pairs naturally with 体力.

prompt.context_jp: 「あの足袋屋 ＿＿＿＿だ 潰せ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの足袋屋　＿＿＿＿　だ、潰せ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word for 'an eyesore / in the way'.

feedback.correct_en: 目障り means 'an eyesore / something that irritates by being in view' — exactly Kohara's hostile dismissal of the tabi shop.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目立ち means 'standing out' (neutral), and 目先 means 'immediate / short-sighted'. Neither carries the aggressive-nuisance tone.

prompt.context_jp: このソールも このアッパーも ＿＿＿＿の最高のランニングシューズだと思います
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿＿＿　の最高のランニングシューズだと思います。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the four-character phrase meaning 'one of a kind / unique'.

feedback.correct_en: 唯一無二 means 'one and only, without a second' — Mogi declares the Rikuoh truly unique.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一期一会 is 'once in a lifetime encounter' (meetings), and 十人十色 is 'to each their own'. Neither describes uniqueness of an object.

prompt.context_jp: 焦っても結局は損をするだけだと自分に＿＿＿＿ながら
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分に　＿＿＿＿　ながら。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb for 'telling oneself / persuading oneself'.

feedback.correct_en: 自分に言い聞かせる is the fixed expression for 'telling oneself / convincing oneself' — Miyazawa is trying to calm himself inwardly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話しかける and 呼びかける both mean to address someone else; they don't convey the inward-directed self-persuasion needed here.

prompt.context_jp: The commentator is announcing the sash about to be passed to Mogi.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds the most natural as a live sports announcement?

choices.text: 茂木裕人に これから たすきが渡ります
茂木裕人へ これから たすきを渡られます
茂木裕人を これから たすきが渡ります

feedback.correct_en: 渡る is intransitive — the sash passes TO Mogi. に marks the recipient and たすき takes が as the subject that moves.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses an awkward passive 渡られます that mangles the construction. C mistakenly puts を on the human recipient, which isn't how 渡る works.

contrast_examples.jp: バトンが次の走者に渡る。
contrast_examples.en: The baton passes to the next runner.
Hand the baton to him (transitive 渡す).

prompt.context_jp: Iiyama, confident in Mogi, replies to a worried comment.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Iiyama's confident, casual reassurance?

choices.text: 大丈夫だ 俺には分かるんだ
大丈夫です 私には分かります
大丈夫だ 俺で分かるんだ

feedback.correct_en: Iiyama is a gruff older craftsman; plain-form だ with 俺 and 'に (experiencer) + 分かる' fits his register perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: B over-polishes him into desu/masu with 私, out of character. C uses で instead of the standard に for the experiencer of 分かる.

prompt.context_jp: Mogi pledges to repay Kohaze-ya by winning more races.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds the most natural for Mogi's promise?

choices.text: 今度は 俺が こはぜ屋さんの力になりますから
今度は 俺が こはぜ屋さんの力をなりますから
今度は 俺で こはぜ屋さんの力になりますから

feedback.correct_en: 力になる ('become someone's strength / be of help') takes の to mark whose help it is, and が for the one doing it. This is the stock phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: B wrongly uses を with なる (which never takes を for its complement). C uses で instead of が, which weakens 'I'll be the one' to a vague means.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたの力になりたい。
contrast_examples.en: I want to be of help to you.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が力になってくれた。
contrast_examples.en: He was a source of support.

prompt.context_jp: Miyazawa's resolve: they have to keep winning and be recognized as the real thing.
prompt.prompt_en: Which rendering sounds the most natural?

choices.text: 勝ち続けて 本物だと認めさせるしかねえんだよ
勝ち続いて 本物だと認めさせるしかねえんだよ
勝ち続けて 本物だと認めるさせるしかねえんだよ

feedback.correct_en: 勝ち続ける (compound verb) te-form is 勝ち続けて. 認めさせる is the correct causative of 認める ('make them recognize').
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 続いて (intransitive) which doesn't take an object like 勝ち. C mangles the causative by inserting る before させる.

contrast_examples.en: The rain keeps falling (intransitive 続く).

prompt.context_jp: The gruff old advisor shows up at the race and Miyazawa scolds him for coming.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best preserves the casual, blunt tone of the exchange?

choices.text: ダメだよ こんなとこ来ちゃ
いけませんよ こんな所にいらっしゃっては
ダメだよ こんなとこ来ては

feedback.correct_en: The scene is intimate and casual: contracted とこ and 来ちゃ (from 来ては) match Miyazawa's warm scolding of his old mentor.
feedback.incorrect_en: B shifts to full keigo, which clashes with their familiar relationship. C uses the uncontracted 来ては, which sounds stiffer than the lived-in 来ちゃ.

contrast_examples.jp: いらっしゃってはいけません。
